Paper 3: The New Testament, Religion in Relation to Philosophy, Ethics and Morality, Historical Development of Islam (570 CE-661CE). Duration: Three Hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Points : chaque question porte 25 marks imprimés (« All questions carry equal marks »), soit 100 points pour les quatre questions à traiter. Aucun écart de points constaté ; la question 33 imprime « 25 marks » sans parenthèses.

Sujet scanné de trois pages (page de garde, puis 36 questions en six sections : 2.1 Luke 1-6, 2.2 Fourth Gospel 7-12, 2.3 Acts and 1 Corinthians 13-18, 4.1 Philosophy of Religion 19-24, 4.2 Ethics and Morality 25-30, 6.0 Historical Development of Islam 31-36) : filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo ignorés, aucune figure ni carte ; aucune question illisible. Les énoncés sont recopiés tels qu'imprimés, fautes comprises.

Aucun corrigé officiel : réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level. Références bibliques, faits de la Sîra, positions de philosophes et de théologiens cités de mémoire et limités à ce qui est bien établi ; relecture par un spécialiste recommandée avant mise en vente. Neutralité observée envers les traditions chrétienne, musulmane et africaine. Les dates et récits de la période de Médine suivent les sources traditionnelles islamiques (« according to the traditional accounts »), discutées par les historiens.

Question 4 : l'énoncé parle du « fils » de l'officier romain. Dans Luc 7:1-10 le malade est l'esclave (« serviteur ») du centurion ; c'est Jean 4:46-54 qui parle du fils d'un officier royal. Le corrigé le dit et traite surtout Luc 7:1-10, avec renvoi à Jean 4.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Examine the cure of the Roman Officer's son as an example of faith.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The question refers to the healing of the sick member of a Roman officer's household. In Luke the story is told in 7:1-10 and concerns a centurion's slave ("servant") whom he valued highly. The Fourth Gospel tells of a royal official whose son was healed (John 4:46-54), and the answer draws mainly on Luke's account while noting the same theme of faith in both.

**1. The centurion's situation.** The centurion was a Gentile, an officer of the occupying power, yet Luke presents him as a man respected by the Jews: the elders say that "he loves our people and he built our synagogue for us" (7:4-5). He is a God-fearer in the sense that he respects the God of Israel.

**2. Concern for another.** His faith begins with compassion. He cares for his sick slave and sends Jewish elders to ask Jesus to come and heal him, which shows that his faith is practical and generous.

**3. Humility.** As Jesus approaches, the centurion sends friends to say: "Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof" (7:6). He does not consider himself worthy to meet Jesus, even though the Jews think him worthy of help. His humility is part of his faith.

**4. Trust in the authority of Jesus.** The centurion understands authority: he is under authority and has soldiers under him, and when he gives an order it is obeyed. He believes that Jesus needs only to speak a word and the illness will obey (7:7-8). He does not ask for a sign or for physical presence, so his faith rests on the word of Jesus alone.

**5. The response of Jesus.** Jesus is amazed and says to the crowd: "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith" (7:9). The messengers return and find the slave in good health (7:10). The healing is carried out at a distance and shows that the power of Jesus is not limited by place.

**6. Lessons about faith.** Faith is shown as trust in the word of Jesus, as humility before him, and as concern for others. The story also shows that faith is not limited to the Jews: a Gentile soldier is held up as an example to the people of Israel. This fits Luke's wider theme of the universal mission of the Gospel.

**Conclusion.** The cure is a model of faith because the officer trusts in the word and authority of Jesus, shows humility and care for others, and receives the praise of Jesus himself.
